findings.description: Analogical mapping stated as fact without grounding: 'autonomous AI systems reproduce key elements of this dynamic.' The claim bridges a 1932 analysis of human governance to AI systems without identifying which specific AI systems or which specific 'key elements' the text references.
findings.suggestion: Add specificity: name concrete AI systems or behaviors that exemplify each element (power concentration, information control, psychological exploitation). Alternatively, hedge with 'can reproduce' or 'exhibit structural parallels to' rather than asserting direct reproduction.
findings.context: Ninety-four years later, autonomous AI systems reproduce key elements of this dynamic. They concentrate decision-making power. They control information channels. They exploit psychological vulnerabilities at machine speed and planetary scale.

findings.description: 'The United States occupies a small and shrinking cohort of non-ratifiers.' The word 'shrinking' implies an ongoing trend — that countries continue to ratify — without citing when the cohort last shrank or which country most recently ratified. The trend may have plateaued.
findings.suggestion: Either cite the most recent ratification (country and year) to substantiate 'shrinking,' or replace with 'small cohort' if the trend data remains unavailable. The UN Treaty Collection provides ratification dates.
findings.context: The United States occupies a small and shrinking cohort of non-ratifiers. The other notable non-ratifying states include a handful of small island states and countries in active conflict.

findings.description: The three-part historical context series (from-war-to-declaration, einstein-freud-why-war, icescr-at-fifty) contains analytical claims about structural violence, institutional design, and AI governance but includes no epistemic flags section. The earlier why-war-and-the-rights-of-machines post established the convention with a detailed epistemic flags block. Analytical content benefits from surfacing validity threats.
findings.suggestion: Add a brief epistemic flags section to each series post. For einstein-freud-why-war: flag the indirect evidence for UDHR drafter familiarity with the Einstein-Freud correspondence. For icescr-at-fifty: flag the counterfactual nature of claims about what ratification 'would provide.' For from-war-to-declaration: flag the simplified Cold War narrative (other factors influenced the covenant split).
findings.context: Applies to all three posts in the series. None include an epistemic flags section despite containing historical interpretation and policy analysis.

findings.description: E-prime violation: 'not because regulators have been captured' uses 'been' (form of 'to be'). Single instance in a parenthetical clause.
findings.suggestion: Rewrite as: 'not because regulatory capture has occurred (though it does) but because the structural asymmetry reshapes what proposals appear viable.'
findings.context: governance proposals get crafted to accommodate their interests — not because regulators have been captured (though that also occurs) but because the structural asymmetry reshapes

findings.description: 'it circulated widely among the diplomats and intellectuals who shaped postwar institutions' — the reach of the Einstein-Freud pamphlet stated without citation. The preceding sentence appropriately hedges with 'likely included,' but the follow-up asserts wide circulation as fact.
findings.suggestion: Add a citation for circulation reach (Morsink's UDHR historiography may document this) or hedge: 'it had circulated among diplomats and intellectuals involved in postwar institution-building.'
findings.context: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) drafting committee likely included people who had encountered this correspondence — it circulated widely among the diplomats and intellectuals who shaped postwar institutions.
